description.en: It occupies the Palau Nacional, the monumental building that has presided over Montjuïc since the 1929 exhibition, and it holds a thousand years of Catalan art. What almost nobody expects is the Romanesque hall: wall paintings lifted from Pyrenean churches and remounted on replicas of their apses, so you see them as they were meant to be seen. Then come the Gothic rooms, the Renaissance, Gaudí and the modernists, and a photography collection that tends to go unnoticed. The entrance staircase is, on its own, one of the best viewpoints in the city, and it is open to anyone.

whyWorthIt.es: Las pinturas románicas del Pirineo, remontadas sobre sus ábsides, no se ven así en ningún otro sitio.
whyWorthIt.en: Pyrenean Romanesque wall paintings, remounted on their apses, are not shown like this anywhere else.

transit.en: Espanya metro (L1, L3, L8), then a 700 m climb up the staircase.
